subject: Pricing sensitivity & follow-up: tradeoffs and next steps with KestrelPay
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@kestrelpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing sensitivity & follow-up: tradeoffs and next steps with KestrelPay

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Top pain points you shared
- Token spend variability: spikes from peak-day batch inference (auth/clearing flows) are the main driver of unpredictable monthly spend.
- Latency requirement: 150ms P95 end-to-end on the fraud-check path; anything above 200ms risks user drop-off.
- Budget guardrails: finance has flagged a strict monthly ceiling for proofs-of-concept (PoC) and requires a 12-month TCO to approve any reserved capacity.
- Compliance: logs and audit retention need to be exportable for procurement; potential HIPAA adjacency for certain data fields.

Goals you want to validate in the PoC
- Demonstrate a repeatable per-request cost at or below $0.004 per inference in steady state (target).
- Keep 95th latency below 150ms for the primary route.
- Show a 35–50% reduction in token cost relative to the naive baseline via batching + KV caching.

Levers we discussed (short form)
- Dynamic batching on inference gateway (saves ~25–40% on per-token cost depending on concurrency).
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context slices (saves 20–60% on common flows).
- Model variant routing: route low-latency requests to smaller 8-bit quantized variants; route quality-critical flows to full precision.
- Reserved capacity for predictable throughput once volume is validated; reduces per-token price but requires a commit.

Proposed next steps
1) I’ll attach a conservative 12-month TCO sketch (attached: redwood-cost-breakdown.xlsx) and a short playbook for batching/caching options (attached).
2) Internal: Ben will scope a quick config proposal (batching targets, cache TTLs, model mapping) and an ops runbook for rollout.
3) You: confirm a sample 2-week production trace (anonymized) or a representative traffic CSV so we can model expected batching gains.
4) Schedule: suggest a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through the TCO assumptions and procurement asks.

Attachment: redwood-cost-breakdown.xlsx (conservative and upside scenarios)
Attachment: batching-playbook.pdf (examples and config templates)

Thanks again — I’ll flag Ben on numbers below.

— Ava
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@kestrelpay.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@kestrelpay.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sensitivity & follow-up: tradeoffs and next steps with KestrelPay

Ava — thanks for the clear summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement will require a 12-month TCO that separates infrastructure/utilization discounts from any reserved-contract discounts. Can you make the conservative case (no reserved commit) and an optimistic case (6–12 month commit)?
- We have a strict monthly cap for PoC projects of $25k — finance will not approve >$25k unless we get EVP sign-off. Please show the PoC cost within that boundary (conservative scenario).
- We can provide an anonymized 10k-row trace for your modeling next week.
- Security/compliance: we need to confirm that audit logs can be exported in a format our audit team accepts (CSV/JSON) — please cc security if that requires more detail.

Also, curious if the batching numbers you mentioned assume 50ms mean queue time. If batching adds more queue time in our production peak, it could push P95 above the target; we need a breakdown of latency/cost tradeoff per batching window.

Happy to take the follow-up next Tue/Thu AM PT.

— Samir
Director, Platform Engineering | KestrelPay
samir.gupta@kestrelpay.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@kestrelpay.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sensitivity & follow-up: tradeoffs and next steps with KestrelPay

Samir — quick notes against your asks and a conservative modeling approach: 

- TCO scenarios: we’ll produce three lines in the workbook:
  * Conservative (no reserved commit, on-demand/hosted pricing, pessimistic traffic tail)
  * Moderate (short reserved slab for peak hours, modest caching assumptions)
  * Optimistic (12-month commit + aggressive caching/batching numbers)

- PoC sizing & $25k cap: if you aim to keep PoC <= $25k we recommend starting with a 30-day focused test on the highest-value route (the fraud-check path). We model that at ~50k requests/mo and show cost sensitivity to batching windows (5ms / 20ms / 50ms). I’ll include a sensitivity table.

- Latency math: batching gains generally assume a mean queue of 10–30ms for high-concurrency windows. For your P95 requirement we’ll provide the incremental queue latency per batching window and a mapping to whether the request is routed to the low-latency variant (no queue) vs. batched path.

- Audit logs: Monica — can you confirm log export formats and retention options?

I’ll attach an initial sensitivity table to the Drive folder and have the workbook updated by Monday EOD PT.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 May 2028 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sensitivity & follow-up: tradeoffs and next steps with KestrelPay

Thanks Samir — perfect. Confirming next concrete steps and owners: 

1) Ben: publish the conservative/moderate/optimistic TCO sheets to the shared Drive by Mon EOD (will call out $25k PoC constraint).
2) Monica (security): drop a short note on acceptable audit export formats and whether additional SOC2 evidence is needed for procurement.
3) KestrelPay: please upload the anonymized 10k-row trace to the Drive link above (I’ll share a sanitized template).
4) Follow-up call: Tue 23 May 2028, 09:30 PT — 30 minutes to review TCO and procurement asks (I’ll send calendar invite once Ben confirms workbook).

If anything changes on the budget side before Monday, flag it and we’ll re-scope the PoC to a narrower route.

Thanks again — looking forward to the trace and to getting you a clear, conservative TCO.

— Ava
